title: Does pre-warming the connection actually help?
hypothesis: A pre-warmed keep-alive socket beats opening the connection at fire time, because the TCP handshake is paid before the drop instead of inside the fire window.
method: Same HTTP-direct bot, one variable: warm pre-opens the fire socket before the drop; cold opens it after detecting release. Loopback, single-clock release->hit.
conclusion: Pre-warming wins — ~26% lower median (warm ~1.10 vs cold ~1.48 ms). Even on loopback, where a TCP connect is nearly free, opening the socket inside the fire window still costs ~0.4 ms. On a real TLS endpoint that gap is a full handshake (tens of ms), so warming is decisive.
decision: Always pre-warm the fire connection before the drop; cold-connect is never worth it.
